questions.prompt: What accounting tells a business — Does collecting an old credit sale create new revenue?
options: Collecting the receivable swaps one asset for another.
Every cash receipt is sales revenue.
questions.explanation: Revenue was earned when the original sale occurred; collection reduces the amount owed by the customer.

questions.prompt: What accounting tells a business — Explain the accounting consequence: which statement fits this lesson?
options: All debit entries reduce assets.
Revenue was earned when the original sale occurred; collection reduces the amount owed by the customer.
The timing of cash always determines the timing of profit.
questions.explanation: Collecting the receivable swaps one asset for another.

questions.prompt: What accounting tells a business — In the model “Three different accounting questions”, what belongs to “Performance”?
options: Resources and claims at a date
Money available to pay debts
Income less expenses over a period
questions.explanation: Performance: Income less expenses over a period. Trace this relationship through the worked example.

questions.prompt: What accounting tells a business — In the model “Three different accounting questions”, what belongs to “Position”?
options: Resources and claims at a date
Money available to pay debts
Income less expenses over a period
questions.explanation: Position: Resources and claims at a date. Trace this relationship through the worked example.

questions.prompt: Conventions, business law and ethical choices — Explain the accounting consequence: which statement fits this lesson?
options: All debit entries reduce assets.
Legal form determines owner liability; a trading name alone does not change it.
The timing of cash always determines the timing of profit.
questions.explanation: A registered name is not a separate legal company.

questions.prompt: Internal control across business assets — Explain the accounting consequence: which statement fits this lesson?
options: The timing of cash always determines the timing of profit.
All debit entries reduce assets.
A risk reduction system must be reviewed and supplemented with evidence.
questions.explanation: Controls reduce risk but remain subject to collusion, override and error.

questions.prompt: Credit purchases and creditor payments — Explain the accounting consequence: which statement fits this lesson?
options: The purchase was recognised when the goods and obligation were recorded.
The timing of cash always determines the timing of profit.
All debit entries reduce assets.
questions.explanation: Supplier payment settles the existing payable.

questions.prompt: Funding a small business — Explain the accounting consequence: which statement fits this lesson?
options: All debit entries reduce assets.
Fees, interest, risk, security and future payments must also be compared.

questions.prompt: Cash and credit sales under perpetual inventory — Explain the accounting consequence: which statement fits this lesson?

All debit entries reduce assets.

questions.prompt: Closing income, expenses and drawings — Explain the accounting consequence: which statement fits this lesson?
options: All debit entries reduce assets.
Closing resets period performance accounts rather than disposing of resources.
The timing of cash always determines the timing of profit.
questions.explanation: Permanent asset and liability accounts carry their balances forward.

questions.prompt: Writing off an irrecoverable account — Explain the accounting consequence: which statement fits this lesson?
options: The timing of cash always determines the timing of profit.
All debit entries reduce assets.

questions.prompt: Drawings of cash and inventory — Explain the accounting consequence: which statement fits this lesson?
options: The entity convention separates owner consumption from business performance.
The timing of cash always determines the timing of profit.
All debit entries reduce assets.

questions.prompt: A classified sole-trader income statement — Explain the accounting consequence: which statement fits this lesson?

The timing of cash always determines the timing of profit.
questions.explanation: Borrowing increases a liability and cash rather than revenue.

questions.prompt: Customer receipts and receivable control — Explain the accounting consequence: which statement fits this lesson?
options: The timing of cash always determines the timing of profit.
All debit entries reduce assets.
The sale date and collection date need not fall in the same reporting period.
questions.explanation: Receipts can collect old invoices and leave new invoices outstanding.

questions.prompt: GST categories and inclusive prices — Explain the accounting consequence: which statement fits this lesson?
options: The inclusive total contains eleven equal parts: ten price parts and one GST part.
The timing of cash always determines the timing of profit.
All debit entries reduce assets.
questions.explanation: The GST component of a 10% GST-inclusive total is total ÷ 11.

questions.prompt: Posting and balancing ledger accounts — Explain the accounting consequence: which statement fits this lesson?
options: All debit entries reduce assets.
Both increases and decreases must be included before the net balance is reported.
The timing of cash always determines the timing of profit.
questions.explanation: A balance is the difference between the two sides, labelled debit or credit.

questions.prompt: Trial balance and errors — Explain the accounting consequence: which statement fits this lesson?
options: The timing of cash always determines the timing of profit.
All debit entries reduce assets.
A complete omission affects neither column and therefore leaves equality unchanged.

questions.prompt: Correcting journal and ledger errors — Explain the accounting consequence: which statement fits this lesson?
options: Repeating an already correct Bank entry creates a new error.
The timing of cash always determines the timing of profit.
All debit entries reduce assets.
questions.explanation: Correct only the accounts or amounts that differ from the required entry.

questions.prompt: Capital, cash purchases and cash expenses — Explain the accounting consequence: which statement fits this lesson?
options: All debit entries reduce assets.
Classify what is acquired and whether it has been consumed before recording.
The timing of cash always determines the timing of profit.
